headline: Nvidia's earnings beat snaps the AI selloff, Anthropic IPO looms
body: Futures are pointing solidly higher into today's open, with S&P 500 contracts up roughly 0.5-0.7% and Nasdaq-100 futures gaining closer to 1%, as Nvidia's quarterly report and above-consensus guidance gave a battered AI trade something to rally around. The bounce follows three straight down sessions that at one point took the Nasdaq down 2.5% in a single day and pushed the VIX above 23 — its highest close in roughly two weeks — as investors grew nervous that AI-linked valuations and spending plans had outrun the underlying fundamentals. Nvidia shares rose nearly 4% in premarket trading on the back of the print, and that relief is spilling into chip, cloud, and power names that had been sold hardest on the way down, turning what had been a tech-led risk-off stretch into a broader, if still tentative, risk-on morning.

The next catalyst is Anthropic's IPO, expected to price this evening and begin trading tomorrow under the ticker ANT, with order books reported running several times oversubscribed from institutional buyers and a valuation push toward the trillion-dollar range. That scale of demand is one of the clearer signals that large allocators are still willing to pay up for AI exposure even after a rough stretch for the sector. Retail positioning looks more split: one poll found a majority of respondents don't plan to buy into the IPO directly, even as sentiment readings on broad index trackers like SPY and QQQ stay tilted bullish and AI-compute-adjacent names see active chatter. Read together, it's a market leaning on one earnings print and one listing to settle whether AI conviction has returned, or just the bounce.
